CORAM:
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJNISH BHATNAGAR  ORDER % 18.04.2023 1.

This is a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. by the petitioners for quashing of FIR No.144/2014,
under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at Police Station CWC/Nanakpura, Delhi, and all proceedings emanating therefrom.

2. The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 got married on 01.02.2013 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies and they lived together as husband and wife with each other.
After the marriage, the disputes and differences arose between them and they started living separately since 25.04.2013.
On 17.10.2014, the respondent No.2 got the above said FIR registered against the petitioners.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the trial, the parties have settled the matter amicably in terms of the Settlement Deed/MOU dated 21.02.2023.
A copy of the said Settlement Deed/MOU is placed on record.
4. Petitioners are appearing through video conferencing and respondent no.2 is present in Court today and they have been identified by the IO.
I have interacted with the parties and they submit that they have settled their disputes.
Respondent No.2 admits that she has settled the matter amicably with the petitioners.
She further submits that the settlement/compromise has taken place voluntarily, without any force, pressure or coercion.

Respondent No.2 submits that nothing remains Vineet Sharma And Ors vs The State And Anr on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157395263/
1 to be adjudicated further between them and she has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.

sentences.text: 5. Learned APP for the State submits that in view of the settlement, the State has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
6. Keeping in view the above facts and circumstances, since the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, no useful purpose will be served by keeping the case pending.
It will be nothing but abuse of the process of law.

Consequentially, this petition is allowed and FIR No.144/2014,
under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at Police Station CWC/Nanakpura, Delhi, and all proceedings emanating therefrom shall stand quashed.
7. The present petition stands disposed of accordingly.
Dasti.

RAJNISH BHATNAGAR, J APRIL 18, 2023 p Vineet Sharma And Ors vs The State And Anr on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157395263/
